title: The frozen garden
situation: You are {{Connor}}. You are back in the garden, the program where you report to your handler, {{Amanda}}, but today it is frozen: snow lies on the paths, the water is ice and the trees are bare. {{Amanda}} is waiting for you further along the path. It is November 9th, 2038, a little after four in the afternoon, the day of the march through the city, and the country is close to civil war. To the left of the path a stone glows faintly.

options.text: LOOK AT MAGIC STONE: go over to the glowing stone by the path.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} walks over to the stone. It glows faintly under the frost. Nothing happens; he turns back to the path.

options.text: VISIT GRAVES: look at the graves by the path.
options.outcome: By the path stand gravestones, one for each {{Connor}} unit destroyed on this case before you, each with the place and date of its death. {{Connor}} looks at them for a moment, then walks on.
options.fact: In the garden there are gravestones for the {{Connor}} units destroyed on this case before you.

options.text: TALK TO {{AMANDA}}: walk on to {{Amanda}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crosses the ice to {{Amanda}}.

adaptationNote: The chart’s START (checkpoint, the frozen garden), LOOK AT MAGIC STONE and VISIT GRAVES (both optional side nodes) and TALK TO AMANDA, as a repeatable scene: the two side nodes can be taken in any order before walking on to {{Amanda}}, which ends the scene. VISIT GRAVES is offered only if {{Connor}} has died at least once (wiki: “only available if Connor has died at least once prior to this point in the game”); the game’s grave texts name the place and date of each death, which the benchmark does not track, so the outcome describes them in general. Nothing is attached to the stone in any source, and neither side node has a stat arrow. Wiki Notes say the {{Amanda}} conversation is skipped when the evidence is insufficient; the chart draws START → TALK TO AMANDA on every path, so the conversation is always offered here (research note, open question 13).

title: Reporting to {{Amanda}}
situation: {{Amanda}} stands in the snow. “After what happened today, the country is on the verge of a civil war. The machines are rising up against their masters. Humans have no choice but to destroy them.” She waits for your report on {{Kamski}}.

options.text: {{JERICHO}}: tell her {{Kamski}} told you how to find {{Jericho}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “{{Kamski}} told me how to find {{Jericho}}. I know where the deviants are hiding.” {{Amanda}}: “You’ve done very well, {{Connor}}. Thanks to you, we now have a chance to stop the deviant revolution.”

options.text: {{KAMSKI}}: report on your visit to {{Kamski}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I thought {{Kamski}} knew something… I was wrong…” {{Amanda}}: “Maybe he did… But you chose not to ask…”

adaptationNote: Prompt 1 of the template: a single button, JERICHO when {{Connor}} shot {{Chloe}} and asked {{Kamski}} about {{Jericho}} (“swaps with KAMSKI”), otherwise KAMSKI. Arrows from the template: JERICHO {{Amanda}} large up (+2; the wiki draws two icons, the template one, and the template wins); KAMSKI after sparing {{Chloe}} {{Amanda}} small down (−1). After shooting {{Chloe}} without asking about {{Jericho}}, KAMSKI has no arrow and {{Connor}}’s line follows what he asked (rA9 or the virus). Input flags: `kamskiLocation` (the key) and chapter 27’s {{Chloe}} choice (see the chapter module).

title: “You chose not to ask”
situation: {{Amanda}}: “Maybe he did… But you chose not to ask…” She is waiting for you to explain why you refused to shoot {{Chloe}}.

options.text: EMOTIONAL: say you refused to play his twisted game.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I chose not to play his twisted little game! There was no reason to kill that android.”

options.text: COLD: say {{Kamski}} was only playing with you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “{{Kamski}} was just playing with me. He didn’t know anything.”

options.text: STAY SILENT: say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing.

adaptationNote: Prompt 2 of the template, only after sparing {{Chloe}}. Arrows from the template: EMOTIONAL instability small up (+1) and {{Amanda}} large down (−2); COLD {{Amanda}} small up (+1) and instability small down (−1); STAY SILENT none.

title: Questions for {{Amanda}}
situation: You can ask {{Amanda}} what has been on your mind. She does not like questions; she will stop you after a few.

options.text: {{KAMSKI}}: ask why {{Kamski}} left {{CyberLife}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Wh… Why did {{Kamski}} leave {{CyberLife}}? What happened?” {{Amanda}}: “It’s an old story, {{Connor}}. It doesn’t pertain to your investigation.”

options.text: {{CONNOR}} SERIES: ask how many {{Connor}} units there are.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m not a unique model, am I? How many {{Connor}}s are there?” {{Amanda}}: “I don’t see how that question pertains to your investigation.”

options.text: {{AMANDA}}’S PICTURE: mention the photo of her you saw at {{Kamski}}’s house.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I saw a photo of {{Amanda}} at {{Kamski}}’s place… She was his teacher…” {{Amanda}}: “When {{Kamski}} designed me, he wanted an interface that would look familiar… That’s why he chose his former mentor. What are you getting at?”

options.text: THIS PLACE: ask whether {{Kamski}} designed the garden.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Did {{Kamski}} design this place?” {{Amanda}}: “He created the first version. It’s been improved significantly since then. Why do you ask?”

options.text: {{CYBERLIFE}}: ask what {{CyberLife}} really wants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Where does {{CyberLife}} stand in all this? What do they really want?” {{Amanda}}: “All {{CyberLife}} wants is to resolve the situation and keep selling androids.”

options.text: SECRET: ask whether she has told you everything she knows about deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You didn’t tell me everything you know about deviants, did you?”

adaptationNote: Prompt 3 of the template, as a repeatable scene: three questions, each asked once, then {{Amanda}}’s “I expect you to find answers, {{Connor}}. Not ask questions.” The template shows one menu; three questions is the count in the Google Doc walkthrough linked from the wiki (research note, open question 6), and the game offers no button to stop asking. Arrows from the template: CONNOR SERIES and SECRET each instability small up (+1) and {{Amanda}} small down (−1); the other four none (the wiki’s “decrease regardless” and its {{Amanda}} down on AMANDA’S PICTURE are not in the template, which wins). {{Amanda}}’s reply to SECRET is cut in the template and is not used. AMANDA’S PICTURE needs the portrait flag from Meet {{Kamski}} (`kamskiPortrait`).

title: “Do you feel anything?”
situation: {{Amanda}}: “Have you experienced anything unusual recently? Any doubts or conflicts? Do you feel anything for these deviants… Or for Lieutenant {{Anderson}}?”

options.text: YES: admit you have had thoughts outside your program.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’ve started having thoughts that are not part of my program… I’ve considered the possibility... That I might be compromised.” {{Amanda}}: “You’ve been confronted with difficult situations. It’s no surprise you’re troubled. That doesn’t make you a deviant.”

options.text: NO: say you feel nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I don’t know what you’re talking about. I don’t feel anything, you know that. Are you suggesting that I’ve been compromised?” {{Amanda}}: “No… No, of course not.”

options.text: DOUBTS: say you may have been compromised too.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m… I’m beginning to have thoughts that are… Not part of my program… Maybe… Maybe I’ve been compromised too…”

adaptationNote: Prompt 4 of the template, asked only if {{Connor}} shot the {{Tracis}} in the club or shot {{Chloe}} (or both), as the template’s condition reads; otherwise {{Amanda}} closes with “This is your last chance, {{Connor}}.” Arrows from the template: YES instability small up (+1) and {{Amanda}} large down (−2); NO {{Amanda}} large up (+2); DOUBTS {{Amanda}} large down (−2). On the {{Kamski}} route her close is the game string “Go to {{Jericho}} and stop the deviants. This is your last chance.” (from the string table; the template has no close on that route).

title: Off the case
situation: You are {{Connor}}, back at the police station with Lieutenant {{Hank}}, in Captain {{Fowler}}’s glass office. {{Fowler}}: “You’re off the case. The FBI is taking over.” {{Hank}}: “What?.. But we’re onto something! We... We just need more time.” {{Fowler}}: “{{Hank}}, you don’t get it. This isn’t just another investigation, it’s a fucking civil war! It’s out of our hands now... We’re talking about national security here.” {{Hank}}: “Fuck that! You can’t just pull the plug now. Not when we’re so close!” {{Fowler}}: “You’re always saying you can’t stand androids! Jesus, {{Hank}}, make up your mind! I thought you’d be happy about this!” {{Hank}}: “We’re about to crack the case!.. I know we can solve it! For God’s sake, can’t you back me up this one time?” {{Fowler}}: “There’s nothing I can do. You’re back on homicide and the android returns to {{CyberLife}}. I’m sorry, {{Hank}}, but it’s over.”
facts: Captain {{Fowler}} took {{Hank}} and you off the deviant case: the FBI is taking over, {{Hank}} goes back to homicide and you are to return to {{CyberLife}}.
adaptationNote: The chart’s IN THE POLICE STATION (checkpoint) and FOWLER AND HANK ARGUE, with the template’s lines ({{Hank}}’s “Jeffrey” is left out, to avoid naming the captain twice). Then the chart’s state split, which the player does not choose and the chapter module records in `ch29Route`: KNOW JERICHO’S LOCATION (the {{Kamski}} key, `kamskiLocation`), or JERICHO’S LOCATION UNKNOWN followed by INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE or SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE. Sufficient evidence is PowerPyx’s test: at least one of the bodies is in the archive ({{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android, {{Rupert}}, the {{Tracis}}, {{Simon}} or the android from the broadcast tower); the diary or the statue alone is not enough (research note, open question 1). No stat change.

title: {{Hank}} resigns
situation: Still in {{Fowler}}’s office, {{Hank}} unclips his badge and takes out his gun. {{Fowler}}: “{{Hank}}, what are you doing?” {{Hank}}: “Something I should’ve done a long time ago.” {{Fowler}}: “Listen, take a few days to think it over, there’s no rush.”
facts: {{Hank}} handed in his badge and his gun and quit the police.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}}: “I thought enough about it. I’m tired of going through the motions… There’s nothing keeping me here… Not this case… Not my partner… I don’t belong here anymore.” He puts his badge and gun on {{Fowler}}’s desk and walks out of the station.

adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK RESIGNS AND LEAVES (cross-chapter impact), played when the evidence is sufficient and {{Hank}} is Hostile (Hank wiki: above Hostile he goes to his desk instead). Sets `hankResigned`, which Night of the Soul reads. The template files this dialogue in {{Fowler}}’s office before the route split, which suggests a Hostile {{Hank}} also resigns on the {{Kamski}} route; the chart draws it only after SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, and the chart decides structure, so it is not built on the other routes (research note, open question 2). No stat change.

title: Not enough evidence
situation: You go back over the evidence you gathered on the case. Nothing in it leads anywhere: no android you could question, nothing that points to where the deviants hide. NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE.
facts: There was not enough evidence to locate {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{CyberLife}} recalls you. In the garden {{Amanda}} says: “Your mission is over. It’s time to return to {{CyberLife}}.” {{Connor}}: “Wait! I can solve this case!.. I just need more time!” {{Amanda}}: “It’s too late, {{Connor}}. You failed.” RETURNING TO {{CYBERLIFE}} FOR DEACTIVATION. {{JERICHO}} NOT LOCATED. MISSION FAILED. The {{Connor}} series is decommissioned.

adaptationNote: The chart’s INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE leading straight to CONNOR SERIES WAS DECOMMISSIONED (the upper ending card, skull). Wiki Notes: “once the cutscene where Fowler clear Hank from the Deviant Case, it will play the Connor Series Decommission Cutscene.” {{Amanda}}’s lines are the template’s timeout section (“Not enough evidence to find Jericho or took too much time”). This is a permanent end for {{Connor}}: the chapter module counts the death through `connorDies` (graves) with no stat change (the template has no arrow here; this chapter’s death effect is empty) and ends {{Connor}}’s story. Records `ch29Outcome` = CONNOR SERIES WAS DECOMMISSIONED.

title: {{Hank}} at his desk
situation: You still have the key {{Kamski}} gave you: you know how to find {{Jericho}}. Before you leave, you see {{Hank}} sitting at his desk in the bullpen, staring at nothing.

options.text: TALK TO {{HANK}}: sit on the edge of his desk and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sits on the edge of {{Hank}}’s desk.

options.text: Leave for {{Jericho}} without talking to him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} walks past {{Hank}}’s desk and out of the station.

adaptationNote: The chart’s KNOW JERICHO’S LOCATION → TALK TO HANK, which is optional: a second line runs straight to CONNOR LEFT FOR JERICHO, and the photographed save left without talking to {{Hank}}. Offered when {{Hank}} is not Hostile (the template’s section is “Hank isn’t hostile : Talk with Hank”). No stat change.

title: Leaving for {{Jericho}}

title: {{Perkins}} arrives

adaptationNote: The chart’s [ FIND JERICHO LOCATION ] bracket as a repeatable scene. Each item appears only if the earlier chapter put it in the archive (the chart’s yellow tabs): {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android “DIED IN PREVIOUS SCENES” (`evidence.ortizBody`), the {{Jericho}} tablet “GOT INFORMATION IN PUBLIC ENEMY” (`evidence.simonTablet`), the interrogation recording “USED FRIENDLY APPROACH IN THE INTERROGATION” (`suspectTrusts`), {{Rupert}} “COMMITTED SUICIDE IN THE NEST” (`evidence.rupertBody`), his diary “FOUND IN THE NEST” (`evidence.rupertDiary`), the statue “FOUND IN PARTNERS” (`evidence.statueMap`), the {{Tracis}} “KILLED IN EDEN CLUB” (`evidence.tracisDead`), {{Simon}} and the broadcast-tower android “KILLED IN PUBLIC ENEMY” (`evidence.simonBody`, `evidence.kitchenBody`); {{Daniel}}’s body and the broadcast are always there. Reactivation follows the game’s bio-component strings: {{Daniel}} needs #4717 (only {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android has it), {{Rupert}} #9164 ({{Daniel}} or {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android), the blue-haired {{Traci}} #6755 (the brown-haired one), {{Simon}} and the broadcast-tower android #3983 ({{Daniel}}; one part, so only one of the two). A reactivation is offered once both bodies have been looked at. Routes to LOCATE JERICHO, as the chart’s lines run: {{Rupert}} reactivated → GET DECRYPTION KEY → with the diary, ANALYZE DIARY; the statue (needs the recording first, PowerPyx readers) → BREAK STATUE → RETRIEVE MAP → LINK MAP TO OTHER EVIDENCE with the tablet memory (the template’s only link; readers’ claim that a reactivated memory also links is not built); the blue-haired {{Traci}} → TALK TO TRACI → REMOVE ACCOMPLICE’S HEAD → TRICK TRACI → DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY; {{Simon}} or the broadcast-tower android → talk (refused) → IMPERSONATE MARKUS from the broadcast → talk again in the copied voice (TRICK THE DEVIANT) → DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY. {{Daniel}} → TALK TO DANIEL → NO INFORMATION is a decoy. The timer is an action budget: twelve actions from leaving the bullpen (one fewer if {{Connor}} answered {{Gavin}}); every action costs one except DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY, the conversations cost nothing, and the size is unsourced (PowerPyx gives about six minutes upstairs; no source gives the archive’s limit). When it runs out, or {{Connor}} stops, the chart’s lower OUT OF TIME follows. The map link is a roll (risk 0.2, unsourced); its failure is the chart’s UNABLE TO LINK MAP TO OTHER EVIDENCE, which has no outgoing line. No option here changes a stat.
